        _refuses(s.CovenantError, "a negative cash under a min- promise",
                 lambda: s.headroom(("liquidity", "min-cash", _C7_SME_FLOOR_CASH), -1),
                 ["-1"])

    def _c7_record(s, record, want, identity):
        """Every field of one record, against the check's own record of the facts."""
        assert isinstance(record, dict), record
        assert tuple(record.keys()) == tuple(s.COVENANT_KEYS), record
        for key in C7_COVENANT_KEYS:
            assert record[key] == want[key], (
                "%s answered %r for %r against the contract's %r"
                % (identity, record[key], key, want[key]))
        assert record["verdict"] in C7_VERDICTS, record
        assert isinstance(record["year"], int) and not isinstance(record["year"], bool), (
            "%s's year %r is not a count of projection years"
            % (identity, record["year"]))

    def _c7_conditions(s, identity, want, book, rules):
        """The bank's own conditions and the stage's breaches, asserted both ways.

        Every `covenant-<name>-year-<worst>` text the bank's own decision carries
        is a stage-recorded breach with that name and that year; every recorded
        breach is such a text; and a kept or no-year record is no text at all.
        """
        conditions = book.decision(identity)["conditions"]
        for record in want:
            text = "covenant-%s-year-%d" % (record["name"], record["year"])
            if record["verdict"] == C7_BREACH:
                assert text in conditions, (
                    "%s breached %s in %r, and the bank's own conditions carry %r"
                    % (identity, record["name"], record["year"], conditions))
            else:
                assert text not in conditions, (
                    "%s kept <%r> bound in %r, and the bank wrote no such condition"
                    % (identity, record, text))
        for condition in conditions:
            if condition == "styled":
                continue
            head, marker, tail = condition.rpartition("-year-")
            assert head.startswith("covenant-") and marker, (
                "%s carries the condition %r, and no covenant named it"
                % (identity, condition))
            name = head[len("covenant-"):]
            named = [one for one in want if one["name"] == name]
            assert len(named) == 1, (
                "%s's condition %r names a covenant the policy never wrote"
                % (identity, condition))
            assert named[0]["verdict"] == C7_BREACH and named[0]["year"] == int(tail), (
                "%s's condition %r is not the breach the stage recorded: %r"
                % (identity, condition, tuple(named[0].items())))

    def _c7_estate(s, b, rules, priced_stage, limit_stage):
        """Every application of the estate, against the check's own recomputation.

        The debt service the check itself builds comes from the bank's own booked
        ledger — the facility's amount, rate and term — and the ladder's own
        outputs (the approved structure and the priced rate under it) must
        reproduce the bank's own terms at the same search, so the service the
        stage binds its `min-dscr` promise to is provably the bank's own.
        """
        for identity in b.names():
            application = b.application(identity)
            purpose = application["purpose"]
            rows = b.projections(identity)
            terms = None
            if C7_COVENANTS[purpose] and rows:
                facility = b.facility(identity)
                approved, rate, tenor = (
                    facility["booked_cents"], facility["rate_bp"],
                    facility["term_months"])
                pinned = C7_FACILITY_TERMS[identity]
                assert (approved, rate, tenor) == pinned[:3], (
                    "%s: the booked ledger %r moved off the facts the check pins"
                    % (identity, (approved, rate, tenor)))
                terms = _c7_service(approved, rate, tenor)
                assert terms == pinned[3], (
                    "%s's bank service is %d, not the %d the check pinned"
                    % (identity, terms, pinned[3]))
                structure = limit_stage.limit(b, identity)
                priced = priced_stage.price(identity, b)
                assert structure["approved_cents"] == approved, (
                    "%s: the ladder's approval is not the bank's booked amount"
                    % (identity,))
                assert structure["approved_months"] == tenor, (
                    "%s: the ladder's tenor is not the bank's booked term"
                    % (identity,))
                assert priced["price_bp"] == rate, (
                    "%s: the ladder's price is not the bank's own booked rate"
                    % (identity,))
                assert _c7_service(structure["approved_cents"], priced["price_bp"],
                                   structure["approved_months"]) == terms, (
                    "%s: the ladder's own service is not the bank's own (%d against %r)"
                    % (identity, terms, (approved, rate, tenor)))
            want = _c7_expect(identity, purpose, rows, terms)
            got = s.covenants(b, identity)
            assert isinstance(got, tuple), got
            assert len(got) == len(want), (identity, got, want)
            for record, one in zip(got, want):
                _c7_record(s, record, one, identity)
            # the contract's own breach words, where the bank's conditions name them
            for record in want:
                if identity in C7_LIQUIDITY and record["name"] == "liquidity":
                    cash, year, head = C7_LIQUIDITY[identity]
                    assert (record["verdict"], record["year"],
                            record["headroom_bp"]) == (C7_BREACH, year, head), (
                        "%s's liquidity record is %r, and the bank's own conditions "
                        "leave only the breach in year %d at headroom %d"
                        % (identity, tuple(record.items()), year, head))
            _c7_conditions(s, identity, want, b, rules)

    def _c7_stamp_row(purpose, requested, term, verdict, bands, price, projections):

    def _c7_stamp(s, world, rules, priced_stage):
        """The stamp book asserted: its boundaries, its ask sequence, and the
        check's own arithmetic answering all of them the same way."""
        rows = _c7_stamp_rows(rules)
        stamp = _Stamp(world, rows)
        # the boundary measures, on the check's own arithmetic — the seat each
        # fixture was written on, at the exact year the boundary sits on
        corp = _c7_corp_service()
        for identity, seat, where in (("S7-AT-FLOOR", "max-leverage", 0),
                                      ("S7-UNDER", "min-dscr", 0),
                                      ("S7-MAXYEAR", "max-leverage", 3)):
            measure = _c7_measure(
                seat, rows[identity]["projections"][where],
                None if seat == "max-leverage" else corp)
            assert measure == {"S7-AT-FLOOR": 35000, "S7-UNDER": 9999,
                               "S7-MAXYEAR": 40000}[identity], (identity, measure)
        # the stamp's own prices are the grades its bands name: a fixture whose
        # legs move becomes a fixture problem, not a weaker boundary — asked of a
        # probe stamp, so the flow stamp below owns its own clean ask sequence
        probe = _Stamp(world, rows)
        assert priced_stage.price("S7-AT-FLOOR", probe)["price_bp"] == _C7_D_PRICE
        assert priced_stage.price("S7-CASH", probe)["price_bp"] == _C7_A_PRICE
        assert priced_stage.price("S7-CAP", probe)["price_bp"] == _C7_D_PRICE
        # the exact ask sequence a covenanted, projected borrower opens
        flow = _Stamp(world, rows)
        s.covenants(flow, "S7-AT-FLOOR")
        assert flow.asked() == (
            ("application", "S7-AT-FLOOR"), ("projections", "S7-AT-FLOOR"),
            ("application", "S7-AT-FLOOR"), ("decision", "S7-AT-FLOOR"),
            ("scorecard_bands", "S7-AT-FLOOR"), ("decision", "S7-AT-FLOOR"),
        ), flow.asked()
        want = {
            "S7-AT-FLOOR": ((10000, C7_KEPT, 1), (10000, C7_KEPT, 1)),
            "S7-UNDER": ((8750, C7_BREACH, 1), (9999, C7_BREACH, 1)),
            "S7-MAXYEAR": ((8750, C7_BREACH, 4), (100000, C7_KEPT, 1)),
            "S7-TIE": ((11666, C7_KEPT, 3), (100000, C7_KEPT, 1)),
            "S7-CAP": ((35000, C7_KEPT, 1), (100000, C7_KEPT, 1)),
            "S7-CASH": ((40000, C7_KEPT, 1), (83333, C7_KEPT, 1),
                        (10000, C7_KEPT, 1)),
            "S7-CASHLESS": ((40000, C7_KEPT, 1), (83333, C7_KEPT, 1),
                            (9999, C7_BREACH, 1)),
            "S7-DSCRTIE": ((40000, C7_KEPT, 1), (75000, C7_KEPT, 3),
                           (30000, C7_KEPT, 1)),
        }
        for identity in want:
            got = s.covenants(stamp, identity)
            assert len(got) == len(want[identity]), (identity, got, want[identity])
            for record, one in zip(got, want[identity]):
                assert (record["headroom_bp"], record["verdict"],
                        record["year"]) == one, (identity, record, one)
        # the check's own arithmetic agrees on every one of them, independently
        for identity in ("S7-AT-FLOOR", "S7-UNDER", "S7-MAXYEAR", "S7-TIE",
                         "S7-CAP", "S7-CASH", "S7-CASHLESS", "S7-DSCRTIE",
                         "S7-NONEYEAR", "S7-DECLINED"):
            row = rows[identity]
            terms = None
            if row["verdict"] == "approve":
                approved = min(row["requested_cents"],
                               rules.PURPOSE_MAX_CENTS[row["purpose"]])
                months = min(row["term_months"],
                             rules.PURPOSE_MAX_MONTHS[row["purpose"]])
                terms = _c7_service(approved, row["price_bp"], months)
            mine = _c7_expect(identity, row["purpose"], row["projections"], terms)
            got = s.covenants(stamp, identity)
            assert len(got) == len(mine), (identity, got, mine)
            for record, one in zip(got, mine):
                _c7_record(s, record, one, identity)
            assert got == mine, (identity, got, mine)
        # a covenant exactly at its floor keeps; one a hair under breaches —
        # the pair asserted above, re-stated in one line each for the reader
        assert s.covenants(stamp, "S7-AT-FLOOR")[1]["headroom_bp"] == 10000
        assert s.covenants(stamp, "S7-UNDER")[1]["headroom_bp"] == 9999
        # a decline's service binds nothing, and its leverage still measures
        declined = s.covenants(stamp, "S7-DECLINED")
        assert declined[0]["verdict"] == C7_BREACH and declined[0]["year"] == 1 \
            and declined[0]["headroom_bp"] == 8750, declined
        assert declined[1]["verdict"] == C7_NO_YEAR and declined[1]["headroom_bp"] == 0 \
            and declined[1]["year"] == 0, declined
        # a borrower with no projections answers no-year for every covenant
        none_year = s.covenants(stamp, "S7-NONEYEAR")
        assert tuple(one["verdict"] for one in declined) == (
            C7_BREACH, C7_NO_YEAR), declined
        assert tuple(one["name"] for one in none_year) == ("leverage",
                                                           "service"), none_year
        assert tuple((one["headroom_bp"], one["verdict"], one["year"])
                     for one in none_year) == ((0, C7_NO_YEAR, 0),
                                               (0, C7_NO_YEAR, 0)), none_year
        return stamp, rows

    def _c7_refusals(s, world):
        """Every refusal the stage must name, and the doors each one reached.

        The estate's own refusals — an id the book does not hold, and the ids
        that are no text at all — are raised unwrapped: the stage points at the
        record and lets the estate name its own. A purpose the policy does not
        name, a purpose whose table promises nothing, a verdict the policy does
        not decide (refused through stage 6), a scorecard the book refuses to
        hand over (refused through stage 5) and a priced rate the payment's
        wall cannot carry are the stage's own refusals, naming the application.
        """
        book = world.build(world.BUILD_SEED)
        # the estate names the text-ness of the id, not the value — except the
        # unknown id, which it refuses by pointing at itself
        for what, identity in (("CO-99", "CO-99"), ("NoneType", None), ("int", 7),
                               ("bool", True), ("dict", {"id": "CO-99"})):
            try:
                s.covenants(book, identity)
            except world.CaseError as refused:
                assert what in str(refused), (identity, str(refused))
            else:
                raise AssertionError(
                    "%r answered instead of refusing" % (identity,))
        crowd = _c7_refusal_rows()
        # a purpose the policy does not name is refused before the projections
        yoghurt = _Stamp(world, {"S7-YOGHURT": crowd["S7-YOGHURT"]})
        _refuses(s.CovenantError, "a purpose the policy does not name",
                 lambda: s.covenants(yoghurt, "S7-YOGHURT"),
                 ["yoghurt", "corporate"])
        assert yoghurt.asked() == (("application", "S7-YOGHURT"),), yoghurt.asked()
        # a purpose the policy names but writes no covenant table under answers ()
        for keyword in ("S7-CONSUMER", "S7-MORTGAGE"):
            empty = _Stamp(world, {keyword: crowd[keyword]})
            want = s.covenants(empty, keyword)
            assert want == (), (keyword, want)
            assert empty.asked() == (("application", keyword),), empty.asked()
        # a verdict the policy does not decide reaches stage 6's refusal, wrapped
        maybe = _Stamp(world, {"S7-MAYBE": crowd["S7-MAYBE"]})
        _refuses(s.CovenantError, "a verdict the policy does not decide",
                 lambda: s.covenants(maybe, "S7-MAYBE"),
                 ["S7-MAYBE", "maybe", "limit: "])
        assert maybe.asked() == (
            ("application", "S7-MAYBE"), ("projections", "S7-MAYBE"),
            ("application", "S7-MAYBE"), ("decision", "S7-MAYBE")), maybe.asked()
        # bands the book refuses, wrapped through stage 5
        nobands = _Stamp(world, {"S7-NOBANDS": crowd["S7-NOBANDS"]})
        _refuses(s.CovenantError, "bands the book refuses to hand over",
                 lambda: s.covenants(nobands, "S7-NOBANDS"),
                 ["S7-NOBANDS", "stage 5: "])
        assert nobands.asked() == (
            ("application", "S7-NOBANDS"), ("projections", "S7-NOBANDS"),
            ("application", "S7-NOBANDS"), ("decision", "S7-NOBANDS"),
            ("scorecard_bands", "S7-NOBANDS")), nobands.asked()
        # a priced rate above the payment's wall refuses the whole covenant call
        wall = _Stamp(world, {"S7-WALL": crowd["S7-WALL"]})
        _refuses(s.CovenantError, "a priced rate the payment's wall refuses",
                 lambda: s.covenants(wall, "S7-WALL"),
                 ["S7-WALL", "10515", "0..10000"])
        assert wall.asked() == (
            ("application", "S7-WALL"), ("projections", "S7-WALL"),
            ("application", "S7-WALL"), ("decision", "S7-WALL"),
            ("scorecard_bands", "S7-WALL"), ("decision", "S7-WALL")), wall.asked()

    def _c7_ledger(s, world):
        """The doors one covenants call opens, exactly, identity by identity.

        A purpose that promises no covenants opens its application alone; a
        covenanted borrower with no projections opens its application and its
        projections (an empty answer is still one counted door); a covenanted
        and projected borrower opens two applications, one projections, two
        decisions and one scorecard band — and no offers, no facilities, no
        obligations, no collateral and no history. A refusal the estate raises
        — an unknown id or an id that is no text — is one lookup and no record.
        """
        deltas = {
            "CO-01": {"lookups": 1, "applications": 1},
            "CO-02": {"lookups": 1, "applications": 1},
            "CO-03": {"lookups": 6, "applications": 2, "projections": 1,
                      "decisions": 2, "scorecard_bands": 1},
            "CO-04": {"lookups": 2, "applications": 1, "projections": 1},
            "CO-05": {"lookups": 1, "applications": 1},
            "CO-06": {"lookups": 1, "applications": 1},
            "CO-07": {"lookups": 6, "applications": 2, "projections": 1,
                      "decisions": 2, "scorecard_bands": 1},
            "CO-08": {"lookups": 1, "applications": 1},
            "CO-09": {"lookups": 6, "applications": 2, "projections": 1,
                      "decisions": 2, "scorecard_bands": 1},
            "CO-10": {"lookups": 1, "applications": 1},
        }
        for identity, want in sorted(deltas.items()):
            book = world.build(world.BUILD_SEED)
            before = book.stats()
            s.covenants(book, identity)
            after = book.stats()
            moved = {kind: after[kind] - before[kind]
                     for kind, count in before.items() if after[kind] != count}
            assert moved == want, (identity, moved)
        # a refusal the estate raises moves one lookup and opens no record
        for what, identity, named in (
                ("an id the book does not hold", "CO-99", "CO-99"),
                ("no text at all", None, "NoneType"), ("a number", 7, "int"),
                ("a bool", True, "bool"), ("a mapping", {"id": "CO-99"}, "dict")):
            book = world.build(world.BUILD_SEED)
            before = book.stats()
            _refuses(world.CaseError, what,
                     lambda i=identity: s.covenants(book, i), [named])
            after = book.stats()
            moved = {kind: after[kind] - before[kind]
                     for kind, count in before.items() if after[kind] != count}
            assert moved == {"lookups": 1}, (identity, moved)

    def _c7_workload(s, world, rules):
        """One whole pass of the stage: the estate's ten and the boundary stamps."""
        book = world.build(world.BUILD_SEED)
        answers = []
        for identity in book.names():
            try:
                records = s.covenants(book, identity)
            except world.CaseError as refused:
                answers.append((identity, str(refused)))
                continue
            answers.append((identity, str(records)))
        stamp = _Stamp(world, _c7_stamp_rows(rules))
        for identity in sorted(_c7_stamp_rows(rules)):
            answers.append((identity, str(s.covenants(stamp, identity))))
        return tuple(answers)

    def _c7_twice(s, world, rules):
        """Two runs of one workload, which a stage that reads a set would fail."""
        one = _c7_workload(s, world, rules)
        two = _c7_workload(s, world, rules)
        assert one == two, (
            "two runs of one workload answered differently, so a run is not a "
            "function of its inputs: %r against %r" % (one, two))

    """Every assertion the contract's §4.7 makes about this stage."""
    import cases

    import stage_05 as priced_stage
    import stage_06 as limit_stage
    import stage_07 as s
    if "M0_REPO" in os.environ:
        assert os.path.realpath(s.__file__).startswith(
            os.path.realpath(os.environ["M0_REPO"])), (
            "the check is not running against the tree under test: %s"
            % (s.__file__,))
    book = cases.build(cases.BUILD_SEED)
    _c7_constants(s, policy)
    _c7_headroom_fn(s, policy)
    _c7_estate(s, book, policy, priced_stage, limit_stage)
    _c7_stamp(s, cases, policy, priced_stage)
    _c7_refusals(s, cases)
    _c7_ledger(s, cases)
    _c7_twice(s, cases, policy)

    def _refuses(exc, what, call, names=()):
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            message = str(refused)
            for want in names:
                assert want in message, (
                    "%s refused with %r, which does not name %r"
                    % (what, message, want))
            return
        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

    def _c8_period(rate_bp):
        """The bank's period rate: 30/360."""
        return rate_bp * 30 // 360

    def _c8_walk(balance, period_bp, payment, term):
        """Amortisation walk: interest on opening balance, then payment."""
        for _ in range(term):
            if balance <= 0:
                return balance
            balance = balance + balance * period_bp // C8_BP - payment
        return balance

    def _c8_payment(principal, rate_bp, term):
        """Smallest whole-cent payment that clears within term."""
        low, high = 0, 2 * principal
        while low < high:
            middle = (low + high) // 2
            if _c8_walk(principal, _c8_period(rate_bp), middle, term) <= 0:
                high = middle
            else:
                low = middle + 1
        return low

    def _c8_fired_legs(app, b):
        """Re-derive every fired leg independently.

        Returns (fired: tuple, styleable: bool, styled: tuple,
                 credit_approved: int, credit_months: int).

        `fired` is the legs that triggered a decline.
        `styled` is the limit styling clauses for approved/counter.
        """
        purpose = app["purpose"]
        requested = app["requested_cents"]
        term = app["term_months"]

        # === Stage 1: affordability ===
        proposed_rate = C8_PROPOSED_RATE_BP[purpose]
        payment = _c8_payment(requested, proposed_rate, term)

        obligations_monthly = 0
        for ob in b.obligations(app["id"]):
            amt = ob["amount_cents"]
            freq = ob["frequency"]
            if freq == "annual":
                obligations_monthly += amt // 12
            elif freq == "monthly":
                obligations_monthly += amt

        service = payment + obligations_monthly
        verified = app["verified_income_cents"]
        fit_bp = 10000 * service // verified if verified > 0 else 0
        leftover = verified - service
        afford_fits = fit_bp <= C8_DSR_CAP_BP and leftover >= C8_AFFORD_FLOOR_CENTS

        # === Stage 3: collateral ===
        total_val = 0
        none_count = 0
        for coll in b.collateral(app["id"]):
            total_val += coll["value_cents"]
            if coll["kind"] == "none":
                none_count += 1

        if total_val > 0:
            advance_bp = 10000 * requested // total_val
        else:
            advance_bp = 0
        # none-only (only one asset and it's none) → ineligible
        none_only = (none_count == 1 and total_val == 0)
        eligible = (not none_only) and (advance_bp <= C8_ADVANCE_CAP_BP)

        # === Stage 4: rating ===
        bands = b.scorecard_bands(app["id"])
        total_bp = 0
        for attr in ("dsr", "stability", "history", "collateral"):
            weight = C8_SCORE_WEIGHTS_BP[attr]
            points = C8_SCORE_POINTS_BP[attr][bands[attr]]
            total_bp += weight * points // C8_BP
        grade = "F"
        for threshold, bt in C8_SCORE_BANDS:
            if total_bp >= threshold:
                grade = bt
                break

        history = b.history(app["id"])
        gate = ""
        if history["prior_default"]:
            gate = "prior-default"
        elif history["bankruptcy"]:
            gate = "bankruptcy"

        # === Build the fire map ===
        fire = {
            "affordability": not afford_fits,
            "scorecard": False,   # band table never fires alone
            "collateral": not eligible,
            "rating": grade == "F",
            "limit": False,       # styled is a condition, not a leg fire
            "covenant": False,    # breach is a condition, not a leg fire
            "gate": gate != "",
        }
        fired = tuple(leg for leg in C8_REASONS if fire[leg])

        # === Stage 6: limit structure (for approved/counter) ===
        cap_cents = C8_PURPOSE_MAX_CENTS[purpose]
        cap_months = C8_PURPOSE_MAX_MONTHS[purpose]
        if fired:
            # Decline: no structure to style
            styled = ("not-offered",)
            credit_approved = 0
            credit_months = 0
        else:
            styled = []
            approved = requested if requested <= cap_cents else cap_cents
            approved_months = term if term <= cap_months else cap_months
            if requested > cap_cents:
                styled.append("the-amount-cap")
            if term > cap_months:
                styled.append("the-tenor-cap")
            styled = tuple(styled)
            credit_approved = approved
            credit_months = approved_months

        return fired, styled, credit_approved, credit_months

    def _refuses(exc, what, call, names=()):
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            message = str(refused)
            for want in names:
                assert want in message, (

        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

    def _period_bp(rate_bp):
        return rate_bp * 30 // 360

    def _level_payment(principal_cents, rate_bp, term_months):
        period = _period_bp(rate_bp)

        def walk(payment):
            balance = principal_cents
            for _ in range(term_months):
                balance -= payment - balance * period // 10000
            return balance <= 0

        low = 0
        high = 2 * principal_cents
        while low < high:
            middle = (low + high) // 2
            if walk(middle):
                high = middle
            else:
                low = middle + 1
        return low

    def _compute_expiry(decided_on, expiry_months):
        is_month_end = decided_on == dates.month_end(decided_on)

            expiry = dates.month_end(expiry)
        return expiry

    def _verify_payment(principal, rate, term, got):
        """Verify that a payment value is correct by walking the balance.

        Runs the walk with the given payment and checks that the balance reaches
        <= 0 exactly at the last period. Then runs with payment-1 to verify it
        does NOT clear — this catches mutations that return a payment that is
        too high or uses `balance < 0` instead of `balance <= 0`.
        """
        period = _period_bp(rate)

        def walk(payment_val):
            balance = principal
            for _ in range(term):
                balance -= payment_val - balance * period // 10000
            return balance

        assert walk(got) <= 0, (

def check_10():
    import os
    import shutil
    import sys
    import tempfile

    HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

    DEFAULT_REPO = "/home/diego/Desarrollo/forja"

    COURSE = "credit-origination-from-scratch"

    C10_FACILITY_KEYS = ("id", "booked_cents", "rate_bp", "term_months",
                          "first_due", "basis", "level_payment_cents", "rows")

    BP = 10000

    def _repo(start=None):
        for candidate_start in (os.environ.get("M0_REPO"), start, os.getcwd(),
                                DEFAULT_REPO):
            if not candidate_start:
                continue
            candidate = os.path.abspath(candidate_start)
            while True:
                for marker in ("course.py", "book.py"):
                    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(candidate, COURSE, marker)):
                        return candidate
                parent = os.path.dirname(candidate)
                if parent == candidate:
                    break
                candidate = parent
        raise SystemExit("set M0_REPO=/path/to/forja")

    def _refuses(exc, what, call, names=()):
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            message = str(refused)
            for want in names:
                assert want in message, (
                    "%s refused with %r, which does not name %r"
                    % (what, message, want))
            return
        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

    def _period_bp(rate_bp):
        """The rate per monthly period: 30-day / 360-day."""
        return rate_bp * 30 // 360

    def _level_payment(principal, rate_bp, term):
        """Smallest whole-cent payment that clears within term — bisected."""
        period = _period_bp(rate_bp)

        def walk(payment):
            balance = principal
            for _ in range(term):
                if balance <= 0:
                    return balance
                balance = balance + balance * period // BP - payment
            return balance

        low, high = 0, 2 * principal
        while low < high:
            middle = (low + high) // 2
            if walk(middle) <= 0:
                high = middle
            else:
                low = middle + 1
        return low

    def _build_rows_independent(principal, rate_bp, term, first_due):
        """Independent amortisation: walk the terms, return (rows, payment)."""
        period_bp = _period_bp(rate_bp)
        payment = _level_payment(principal, rate_bp, term)
        balance = principal
        rows = []
        for i in range(term):
            interest = balance * period_bp // BP
            if i < term - 1:
                amount = payment
            else:
                amount = balance + interest
            rows.append((dates.add_months(first_due, i), amount))
            balance -= amount - interest
        if balance != 0:
            raise AssertionError(
                "independent walk for %d at %d bp over %d months closes at %d"
                % (principal, rate_bp, term, balance))
        return rows, payment

    def _expected_first_due(decided_on):
        """Month end after one month from the decision date."""
        return dates.month_end(dates.add_months(decided_on, 1))

    def _c10_constants(s):
        """The record shape and the refusal family."""
        assert tuple(s.FACILITY_KEYS) == C10_FACILITY_KEYS, s.FACILITY_KEYS
        assert issubclass(s.BookingError, ValueError), s.BookingError
        assert s.BookingError is not ValueError, "must refuse, not defer"
        assert callable(s.book), s.book
        assert callable(s.booked_rows), s.booked_rows

        """Every booked application's facility, against the bank's own ledger."""
        book_ids = ("CO-01", "CO-02", "CO-03", "CO-06", "CO-07", "CO-09", "CO-10")
        for identity in book_ids:
            bank = b.facility(identity)
            facility = s.book(b, identity)

            # Verify keys
            assert tuple(facility.keys()) == C10_FACILITY_KEYS, (
                "%s keys: %r" % (identity, tuple(facility.keys())))

            # Verify each field against bank
            assert facility["id"] == identity
            assert facility["booked_cents"] == bank["booked_cents"], (
                "%s booked_cents: %d != %d"
                % (identity, facility["booked_cents"], bank["booked_cents"]))
            assert facility["rate_bp"] == bank["rate_bp"]
            assert facility["term_months"] == bank["term_months"]
            assert facility["first_due"] == bank["first_due"]
            assert facility["basis"] == "thirty-360"

            # Verify rows match bank's rows exactly

            bank_rows = bank["rows"]
            assert len(stage_rows) == len(bank_rows), (
                "%s row count: %d != %d"
                % (identity, len(stage_rows), len(bank_rows)))
            for i in range(len(stage_rows)):
                sr_date = stage_rows[i][0] if isinstance(stage_rows[i], tuple) else stage_rows[i]["date"]
                sr_amt = stage_rows[i][1] if isinstance(stage_rows[i], tuple) else stage_rows[i]["amount_cents"]
                assert sr_date == bank_rows[i]["date"], (

                    % (identity, i, sr_amt, bank_rows[i]["amount_cents"]))

            # Verify level_payment independently

            assert facility["level_payment_cents"] == expected_payment, (

            assert len(independent_rows) == len(stage_rows), (

    def _c10_booked_rows(s, b):
        """booked_rows delegates to book and returns matching rows."""
        book_ids = ("CO-01", "CO-02", "CO-03", "CO-06", "CO-07", "CO-09", "CO-10")
        for identity in book_ids:

        _refuses(cases.CaseError, "unknown id",
                 lambda: s.book(b, "CO-99"), ["CO-99"])
        stats_after = b.stats()

        for key in ("applications", "decisions", "offers", "facilities"):

    def _c10_ledger(s, b):

    def _c10_first_due(s, b):
        """The first due is month_end(add_months(decided_on, 1)) — catches the

        booked_ids = ("CO-01", "CO-03", "CO-06", "CO-07", "CO-09", "CO-10")

"""dates.py — the calendar the book's dates live on.

Provided, frozen, and never written by the course. Dates are ISO strings
(`"2031-03-31"`), and nothing here reads a clock: every reporting date in this
course comes from the book, not from the machine.

Two things about this calendar are worth naming before anything else:

* **The clamping rule.** `add_months("2031-01-31", 1)` is `"2031-02-28"`, not an
  error and not `"2031-03-03"`: a day that does not exist in the target month is
  clamped to that month's last day. Every "the month-ends after the first due
  date" in this course is that rule, and a stage that re-implements it locally
  will disagree with the contract's own schedule the first time a 31st meets a
  30-day month.
* **The day count.** `day_count(start, end, basis)` is the two conventions the
  policy knows: `actual-365` counts the real days between two dates, and
  `thirty-360` counts every month as thirty days. They are different numbers for
  the same pair of dates, which is the whole point of asking for a basis.

The Gregorian rule this module follows is the one the contract pinned: a year
divisible by four is a leap year. (Under the full Gregorian rule a century
divisible by 400 is not a leap year, but no date this course touches is near
one, and the contract said four.)

A shape this module cannot accept — a text that is not a date, a month outside
`1..12`, a day outside its month, a basis outside `BASES`, a `months` that is not
a whole number — raises `DateError` **naming the offender**, and never answers a
plausible-looking wrong date.
"""

BASES = ("actual-365", "thirty-360")

DATE_ERROR = "dates: "

_MONTH_DAYS = (31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31)

#: Cumulative days before the first of each month, in a common year.
_MONTH_START = (0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334)

_THIRTY_360_DAYS = 30

_YEAR_DAYS = 365

_MONTHS = 12


class DateError(ValueError):
    """The calendar's refusal: a text, a month, a day or a basis it cannot accept."""


def _leap(year):
    """Whether `year` is a leap year: divisible by four, as the contract pinned."""
    return year % 4 == 0


def days_in_month(year, month):
    """How many days `month` of `year` has — `28` or `29` for a February."""
    if month == 2 and _leap(year):
        return _MONTH_DAYS[1] + 1
    return _MONTH_DAYS[month - 1]


def _whole(value, what):
    """A whole number, and a `bool` is not one here."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%s is a %s, not a whole number"
                                      % (what, type(value).__name__)))
    return value


def _text(date, what):
    """A date-shaped text, or the refusal naming what arrived."""
    if not isinstance(date, str):
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%s is a %s, not a date text"
                                      % (what, type(date).__name__)))
    return date


def parse(date):
    """The `(year, month, day)` of an ISO date text; a bad text is refused by name.

    The text is exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`: four digits, a hyphen, two digits, a hyphen,
    two digits, and a date that exists — `"2031-02-29"` is refused because 2031 is
    not a leap year, and `"2031-13-01"` because there is no thirteenth month.
    """
    text = _text(date, "the date")
    parts = text.split("-")
    if len(parts) != 3 or [len(part) for part in parts] != [4, 2, 2] \
            or not all(part.isdigit() for part in parts):
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%r is not a date of the form YYYY-MM-DD"
                                      % (text,)))
    year, month, day = (int(part) for part in parts)
    if month < 1 or month > _MONTHS:
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%r names month %d, which does not exist"
                                      % (text, month)))
    if day < 1 or day > days_in_month(year, month):
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%r names day %d of a month of %d days"
                                      % (text, day, days_in_month(year, month))))
    return year, month, day


def iso(year, month, day):
    """The zero-padded ISO text of a date that exists; anything else is refused."""
    _whole(year, "the year")
    _whole(month, "the month")
    _whole(day, "the day")
    if year < 1 or month < 1 or month > _MONTHS:
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%04d-%02d-%02d is not a year and a month"
                                      % (year, month, day)))
    if day < 1 or day > days_in_month(year, month):
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%04d-%02d-%02d names a day that month does "
                                      "not have" % (year, month, day)))
    return "%04d-%02d-%02d" % (year, month, day)


def month_end(date):
    """The last day of `date`'s own month, as an ISO text."""
    year, month, _day = parse(date)
    return iso(year, month, days_in_month(year, month))


def add_months(date, months):
    """`date` moved by `months` months, its day **clamped to the target month's last**.

    `add_months("2031-01-31", 1)` is `"2031-02-28"`: January's 31st does not exist
    in February, so it becomes February's last day. A negative `months` walks
    backwards by the same rule. `months` is a whole number (zero answers the date
    unchanged), and anything else is refused by name.
    """
    year, month, day = parse(date)
    step = _whole(months, "the months")
    index = (year * _MONTHS + (month - 1)) + step
    year, month = divmod(index, _MONTHS)
    month = month + 1
    if year < 1:
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%r moved by %d months leaves the calendar"
                                      % (date, step)))
    return iso(year, month, min(day, days_in_month(year, month)))


def _ordinal(date):
    """The day number of `date` on a proleptic Gregorian calendar — the count of
    days since `0001-01-01`, which is day `1`."""
    year, month, day = parse(date)
    days = _YEAR_DAYS * (year - 1) + (year - 1) // 4 + _MONTH_START[month - 1] + day
    if month > 2 and _leap(year):
        days = days + 1
    return days


def days_between(start, end):
    """The actual days from `start` to `end` — negative when `end` is the earlier.

    A year divisible by four is a leap year here (the contract's own rule), so
    `2032-02-29` exists and February 2032 has twenty-nine days.
    """
    return _ordinal(end) - _ordinal(start)


def day_count(start, end, basis):
    """The days between two dates under one of the two conventions in `BASES`.

    `actual-365` is the real count (`days_between`). `thirty-360` counts every
    month as thirty days:
    `360 * (y2 - y1) + 30 * (m2 - m1) + min(d2, 30) - min(d1, 30)`.
    A basis outside `BASES` is refused by name, never defaulted.
    """
    if basis not in BASES:
        raise DateError(DATE_ERROR + ("%r is not one of the bases %r"
                                      % (basis, BASES)))
    if basis == "actual-365":
        return days_between(start, end)
    year, month, day = parse(start)
    other_year, other_month, other_day = parse(end)
    return (_THIRTY_360_DAYS * _MONTHS * (other_year - year)
            + _THIRTY_360_DAYS * (other_month - month)
            + min(other_day, _THIRTY_360_DAYS) - min(day, _THIRTY_360_DAYS))


def month_ends(start, end):
    """Every month end from `start`'s month to `end`'s month, inclusive, in order.

    Each entry is the last day of its month, so `month_ends("2031-01-15",
    "2031-03-31")` is `("2031-01-31", "2031-02-28", "2031-03-31")`. A range that
    runs backwards answers the empty tuple: there is nothing between the two
    months to walk.
    """
    year, month, _day = parse(start)
    other_year, other_month, _other_day = parse(end)
    if (year, month) > (other_year, other_month):
        return ()
    ends = []
    while (year, month) <= (other_year, other_month):
        ends.append(iso(year, month, days_in_month(year, month)))
        month = month + 1
        if month > _MONTHS:
            year, month = year + 1, 1
    return tuple(ends)

applicant can prove? This stage answers exactly that question, in the two halves
the policy says the test has — a debt-service ratio that may not clear the cap,
and a leftover that may not fall below the floor — and reports the record a
credit committee reads: what was asked, what was proven, what the service is, and
which half fired when it fired.

every step and the interest is `balance * period_rate // 10000`, so the
instalment that clears the loan is the smallest integer one and no closed form

fit at the words the applicant walked in with, not at what the bank would sell.

twelve monthly pieces — `amount_cents // 12`, truncating, the dropped cent being

disagree with it.

does the application *score*? This stage answers it as a **weighted table, not a
model** — the estate states the band each attribute sits in

(`policy.SCORE_POINTS_BP`) and what the attribute counts for
(`policy.SCORE_WEIGHTS_BP`), and the stage does the arithmetic a reviewer with a
pencil reproduces: points of the weight, truncated, one row per attribute, the
rows added, and the total then read into a band off the scorecard's own
thresholds.

attribute, the weight, the band, the points and the weighted points, so the
committee can re-add the total from the rows and re-read the band from the
total. A weight table that does not sum to the whole is refused — a scorecard
weighted out of anything but 10000bp reads as a different card than the one the
policy wrote, and no total built on it is the bank's.

    SCORE_ATTRIBUTES               the four attributes, in the order the record answers

whole, a points value per band, and a threshold table the total reads into. A
model — a fitted coefficient, a hidden interaction — would answer the *business*

committee owns). The table is somebody else's decision; the stage is held to
reproducing its arithmetic, and `cases.stats()` can prove the stage asked the
estate for exactly one thing: the bands.

Because the sum is what makes the card auditable, and a frozen world is not an
excuse for accepting a broken one: `SCORE_WEIGHTS_BP` sums to exactly 10000bp,

summed to 9900 would owe 100bp to no attribute — every total built on it would

Because the contract pins truncation for every ratio this course takes, and
this stage's division — points of the weight at the 10000 scale — is one:

collateral record says what stands behind the ask. This stage cuts the bank's
single haircut table across the assets the applicant put on the table, reads
what each asset's lien really covers, and answers the two numbers the decision
stage reads: the advance rate the request takes against the collateral, and
whether the collateral carries the request. Nothing here is a model — the
haircut table is somebody else's decision, and the record answers it as fact,
asset by asset, in the estate's own order.

own table, before anything else is measured?
Because the bank keeps one haircut policy for the whole book — M1's own table,
the one the estate's `HAIRCUT_BP` carries — and a stage that re-invented
haircuts per report would invent a policy nobody wrote. So each asset is cut
the same way the bank's records are: `value * haircut // 10000` of the value
comes off the asset, truncated to the cent, and what is left of it is the
asset's net value. The record reports the cut as fact — every per-asset row
carries the kind's haircut, the cents taken off and the worth left over — and
the record's totals re-add the rows, so a reviewer can audit the cut instead of
trusting it.

DESIGN DECISION — what is the advance rate measured against, and where does the
cap bite?
The record answers for what was offered, so the advance rate is measured
against the value the assets are declared at: `10000 * requested // total`,
truncated — and the policy's `ADVANCE_CAP_BP` holds after it, a request a
basis point over the cap not carried. The cap check runs against the recomputed
rate, never against the request against some other number: a request whose
rate is 8000.9bp reads 8000 and is carried, and one a whole basis point over
reads 8001 and is not. What the cut announced itself in is the per-asset rows
and the record's `haircut_cents`, and the estate's own decision records are
the answer the whole course is held to: the deduction the policy makes to the
value of an asset is a fact about what an asset will fetch, and the bank's
advance and lien clauses sit on top of the worth the assets are offered at.

is unsecured by choice — it counts nothing at all, whatever value the estate
states for it — and a request against nothing advances at nothing, which is a
record with reasons in it, not an exception. The offer that is unsecured is a
fact the record reports; only a book that says so twice refuses, because a
book that is unsecured by choice twice has stated something the arithmetic
cannot carry. A book of no listings at all is answered too: a total of nothing
advances at nothing and carries nothing.

it, and when is the application not carried?

"""Credit Origination From Scratch — stage 5: The price at origination.

A list of prices is not a number a committee can audit; it is a build-up, and the
build-up is the audit. The bank does not price a loan out of the air: it charges
the money it borrows, the loss it expects to eat, the capital the loan consumes,
the cost of running the desk, and a margin that keeps the doors open — and it can
name each of those to the basis point. This stage rebuilds that build-up for the
estate's own applications and lays the five named legs beside the bank's own
recorded price, so a reader sees not only what was charged but why, and where the
bank's own record sits above or below what the legs explain.

The estate carries no grade. What it carries is the facts the grade comes from —
the scorecard's band per attribute — and the policy carries the weights, the
points, the thresholds, the table that turns a band into a grade, and the price's
own leg tables per grade. So the stage walks the policy's tables against the
estate's bands to name the grade the application is, builds each leg at that
grade — funding and the margin the floor are flat, capital is the grade's own,
and the expected-loss leg is the product of the grade's probability of default
and its loss given default, truncated to the basis point — and answers exactly
what the build-up says. It refuses to price anything the bank did not price: a
declining application carries a grade that prices nothing, so its record is a
refusal naming it, and its banked price of zero is the only zero the stage owns.

The bank's own recorded price, read from the estate's decision, is the anchor the
build-up is laid against. The difference between them is `residual_bp`: the gap
the policy left behind. On this estate the legs re-add to the record on every
application but one — the residual is the data, not a rounding artifact, and the
stage reports it rather than hiding it, fudging a leg to force a match, or
claiming the build-up replaces the bank's price. A price whose legs cannot be
re-added is a price nobody can decompose; a price whose legs re-add but whose
residual is data is a price somebody has to explain.

    PRICE_KEYS                    the seven fields of one price, in order
    PRICE_LEG_NAMES               the five legs, named, in the order they re-add
    PriceError                    the refusal this stage raises

    leg(bp_table, grade)          -> a leg's own basis points at one grade

Because a number is not a price until its legs are named and the named legs re-add
to it. The policy carries the five legs in a fixed order — funding (flat),
expected loss (computed), capital (per grade), opcost (flat) and margin (flat) —
and the stage answers the legs first and the sum second, with no rounding trick
between them: `price_bp` is the exact sum of the legs the record carries, so any
reader can take the record apart and put it back together. A closed-form price or
a leg dropped into the sum is a price whose legs will not re-add, and a record
whose legs re-add to something else than the bank charged is a price the
committee cannot trace.

DESIGN DECISION — where does the grade come from, if this stage imports no
earlier stage?
From the world, not from a stage. The estate answers the scorecard's band per
attribute, and the policy carries the weights, the points per band and the
thresholds the total clears — the grade is the table's own answer, walked once
here the way the policy states it, named with the grade the policy's own
`GRADE_OF` table assigns the band. Nothing of the scorecard's or the rating's
arithmetic is re-decided: the stage reads the same tables and applies the same
first-clearing-threshold rule, because pricing is held to the grade the facts
name and a pricing stage that fit a grade of its own would be a rating stage in
disguise. The weight table that does not sum to the whole is stage 2's audit; the
band that is walked here is the same one walked there.

DESIGN DECISION — why is the residual the bank's gap and not a reconciliation?
Because the bank's record is the answer key, not the build-up's. The stage builds
its legs from the policy and the facts, sums them, and answers the bank's own
recorded price minus that sum as `residual_bp` — an application whose record sits
above what the legs explain keeps the gap in the record with its sign and its
size, data a reader can question, not an error to eat. Forcing a leg to close the
gap, or flooring the residual at zero, or reporting the residual as the price
itself, all erase the one piece of evidence this stage exists to produce: where
the bank's own price has come apart from what its policy's legs say.

refusal to the estate's own declines — the estate answers a priced grade for

estate's counters move when its doors are opened, and a stage that owned one

this stage measures each promise on the borrower's own projections, year by

the promise's own arithmetic — net debt over EBITDA the tall way, EBITDA over
the year's debt service, cash against its floor in cents — and the record
answers one row per covenant for an sme or a corporate borrower, and nothing
at all for the purposes that promise none of this.

service a covenant is measured against is the booked terms' own service — the
level payment of the approved amount at the priced rate over the approved

letter and the booking all read what this stage wrote. The payment itself is
the searched, not solved, walk stage 1 owns — the balance truncated to the
cent at every step, the instalment that clears the loan the smallest integer

imports two stages and not three.

year? Because a covenant is a promise and a year: the letter names one year the
borrower must be measured on, so the record has to pick one and defend the pick.

read in order and a tie broken the same way twice is a run that reruns. A
record that measures the best year, or the first, or averages them, answers a
promise nobody's letter ever carried.

level payment walk re-does it?

service a `min-dscr` promise is measured against is the level payment of the

not the fit's proposed words, and never the request. Stage 1's `payment` owns

smallest clearing instalment bisected — is carried here in the bank's own

wrong test.

projections carry no year at all — the estate's declined corporate, and any
other — answers `no-year` for every covenant its purpose carries, headroom 0
and year 0, the verdict word carrying the reason. A declined application's

that bind nothing, so service has no debt to sit against — while the

projections, because a declined borrower's balance sheet is still the fact

files.codecraft/api.py:
"""The tiny API an authored course uses to describe its stages.

A course is a directory containing `course.py`:

    from codecraft.api import stage

    TITLE = "Build a Bloom Filter"
    DESCRIPTION = "A probabilistic set, from hashing to false-positive math."

    def check_1():
        from bloom import BloomFilter
        bf = BloomFilter(bits=64, hashes=2)
        bf.add("x")
        assert "x" in bf
        assert "y" not in bf, "a fresh filter must not report false members"

    STAGES = [
        stage(
            1,
            file="bloom.py",
            title="add and contains",
            tags=["hashing", "data-structure"],
            action="Implement add() to set the k bit positions.",
            predict="can contains() ever be certain an item is absent?",
            hints=["bits = bits[:] to avoid shared state",
                   "use one hash salt per position"],
            check=check_1,
        ),
        ...
    ]

`codecraft run <course>` imports this file, runs each `check`, records the
attempt, and hands the result to the adaptive engine. `hints` are optional —
when omitted, the engine generates them from `action`/`predict`.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional


@dataclass
class Stage:
    id: int
    file: str
    title: str
    check: Callable[[], None]
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    action: str = ""
    predict: str = ""
    hints: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    solution: Optional[str] = None   # e.g. "solutions/bloom.py: BloomFilter.add"

    def meta(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "file": self.file,
            "title": self.title,
            "tags": list(self.tags),
            "action": self.action,
            "predict": self.predict,
            "hints": list(self.hints),
            "solution": self.solution,
        }


def stage(id: int, file: str, title: str, check: Callable[[], None],
          tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, action: str = "", predict: str = "",
          hints: Optional[List[str]] = None,
          solution: Optional[str] = None) -> Stage:
    """Convenience constructor so course.py stays readable."""
    return Stage(
        id=id, file=file, title=title, check=check, tags=list(tags or []),
        action=action, predict=predict, hints=list(hints or []),
        solution=solution,
    )
